# Claim disposition — ORION03.NATIVE_TYPED_MERGE_TRANSFER.v1

Terminal: **NATIVE_CROSS_SYSTEM_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL_FROZEN__OUTCOMES_UNRUN**  
`scientific_authority_delta: NONE`  
Novelty authority: `NONE`

## Closed

- Typed parent-witness agreement is explicitly classified as analytic, not empirical detector performance.
- A common native-verifier definition of hybrid authorization is frozen: flat union accepts while both parents reject.
- Three unrelated ecosystems are required: cosign/Sigstore, python-tuf and in-toto, with 10 independent real families each.
- Candidate generation is outcome-blind and targets >=20 tasks/family, >=600 total; synthetic families are controls only.
- Naive union semantics must be native and typed, with component provenance and exact configuration/verifier receipts; an indefensible union yields `CANNOT_CHECK`.
- Every claimed mechanism-localized hybrid requires load-bearing contributions from both parents plus native ablation rechecks.
- Family is the inference unit; all-system support requires hybrids in >=3/10 families and >=1 localized hybrid in each of all three systems.
- Strict-baseline utility requires real loss of parent-authorized objects; convenience/cost cannot substitute.

## Still open

- acquisition and freeze of 30 eligible independent native families;
- >=600 protected native verifier runs;
- empirical hybrid prevalence and localization;
- strict-baseline needless-rejection measurements;
- external peer/novelty authority.

A favourable result would establish cross-ecosystem **non-vacuity of the typed-merge obstruction** under the registered native semantics. It would not turn the analytic typed-witness identity into a learned detector result.
